newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says Jotun field plan submitted.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says Jotun field plan submitted.

text.p: A plan for development and operation of Esso Norway's Jotun oilfield in the North Sea has been submitted to the Norwegian parliament with government backing, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
State-owned Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the scheme involves a jacket-supported wellhead platform tied to a production and storage ship.
"Jotun could help enhance Norway's expertise in building production ships, which has become a speciality for Norwegian industry in recent years," Status Weekly said.

Esso Norge AS said on May 14 it had signed a 300 million crown ($42.6 million) deal with Norway's Haliburton AS for the engineering, procurement, installation and commissioning for the tie-back and pipeline systems of the Jotun.

Oil production from Jotun is due to start in 1999 and to last 16 years. Plateau production will be around 80,000 barrels a day of crude from the years 2000 to 2002, or 2.2 percent of Norwegian oil output, Statoil said.
The Jotun field lies in blocks 25/8 and 25/7, about 200 km west of Stavanger on the west coast of Norway and 29 km north of Esso's Balder field.
The field comprises three separate structures -- Elli, Tau West and Elli South -- which will be developed as one production unit.
Total reserves are estimated at about 200 million barrels of oil equivalent.

Partners in block 25/8 are Esso as operator and Enterprise Oil Norge with 50 percent each. Partners in block 25/7 are Norske Conoco with 37.5 percent, Amerada Hess Norge with 12.5 percent and Statoil with 50 percent.
-- Rolf Soderlind, Oslo newsroom +47 22 42 50 41 ($ = 7.036 Norwegian Crowns)
